questions.question: When steering to avoid a crash, you should:

options.text: Use only one hand to steer.
Keep both hands on the steering wheel.
Not use your mirrors to check other lanes.
Speed up as you get closer to the hazard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep both hands on the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: When turning quickly to avoid hitting something in the road, always keep both hands on the steering wheel. You need a firm grip to turn quickly.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing, you should:

options.text: Speed up to cross the tracks as quickly as possible.
Roll down your window to listen for a train.
Never try to beat an approaching train across the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never try to beat an approaching train across the tracks.
questions.explanation: Slow down as you approach a railroad crossing. You may not hear a train coming. Do not rely only on signals to warn you. Never try to beat a train across the tracks.

questions.question: If you realize you may be running late to your destination, you should:

options.text: Use flashing lights so other drivers move out of your way.
Drive at a safe speed and arrive when you arrive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive at a safe speed and arrive when you arrive.
questions.explanation: Stay calm and accept delays. Avoid dangerous driving. Plan extra time for your trip to help reduce stress about arriving late.

questions.question: When backing up to couple a trailer, you should position the tractor:

options.text: At a 90-degree angle in front of the trailer.
Straight in front of the trailer.
At a 30-degree angle in front of the trailer.
At a 60-degree angle in front of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Straight in front of the trailer.
questions.explanation: Position the tractor straight in front of the trailer when backing up to couple. Backing at an angle can move the trailer and break the landing gear.

questions.question: If you need to add coolant to a system without a recovery tank, you should:

options.text: Keep the vehicle running while adding coolant.
Not wear gloves when touching the radiator cap.
Wait for the engine to cool before adding coolant.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the engine to cool before adding coolant.
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine and let it cool before adding coolant. Wear gloves or use a thick cloth to protect your hands. Turn the radiator cap slowly to the first stop to release pressure.

questions.question: If you must make a quick stop while transporting liquids, one safe option is to:
questions.explanation: If you need to stop quickly to avoid a crash while carrying liquids, use the stab braking method. Do not turn sharply while braking. This can cause your vehicle to tip over, especially vehicles with a high center of gravity.

questions.question: Hydraulic brakes can fail due to:
questions.explanation: Hydraulic brake failure is usually caused by loss of hydraulic pressure. Brakes can also fade from overuse on long downhill grades.

questions.question: Which condition increases a tank's stopping distance?
questions.explanation: Know how long it takes your vehicle to stop. Empty tanks take longer to stop than fully loaded tanks.

questions.question: If confronted by an aggressive driver, you should:

options.text: Try to get out of their way.

questions.explanation: If an aggressive driver confronts you, get out of their way. Avoid eye contact and do not respond to their gestures. Do not speed up or challenge them.

questions.question: When driving a bobtail tractor, you should know that:

options.text: Bobtails cannot drive as fast as tractors with trailers.
Bobtails are harder to stop than tractors with trailers.
Bobtails are illegal in most states.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bobtails are harder to stop than tractors with trailers.
questions.explanation: A bobtail is a tractor without a trailer attached. When driving a bobtail, know that stopping takes longer and more distance than stopping a tractor with a loaded trailer.

questions.question: Your engine runs a pump for compressed gas delivery. After delivery, turn off the engine ____ you unhook the hoses.
questions.explanation: Turn off your engine when loading or unloading a compressed gas tank. If your engine runs a pump, turn it off after the product transfer is done but before you unhook the hoses.

questions.question: After you connect the air lines to the trailer while coupling, you should:
questions.explanation: Following the correct steps to couple and uncouple trailers is important for safe driving. After connecting the air lines to the trailer, supply air to it.

questions.question: To tell the difference between hazardous and non-hazardous materials on a shipping paper:

options.text: Hazardous materials should be listed at the bottom.
Hazardous materials should be listed at the top.
Hazardous materials should be highlighted in the same color as non-hazardous materials.
Non-hazardous materials should be marked with an "X."

questions.correctAnswerText: Hazardous materials should be listed at the top.
questions.explanation: If a shipping paper lists both hazardous and non-hazardous materials, hazardous materials must be set apart in one of three ways: listed first, highlighted in a different color, or marked with an "X" in a column labeled "HM."

questions.question: Poisonous fumes can enter the cab because of:

options.text: Using the wrong type of fuel.

questions.explanation: A broken exhaust system is very dangerous because poisonous fumes can enter the cab or sleeper berth.

questions.question: If the emergency line loses air pressure, it will cause:

options.text: The tractor protection valve to close.

questions.correctAnswerText: The tractor protection valve to close.
questions.explanation: The tractor protection valve keeps air in the trailer's brakes if the trailer breaks away or leaks. When the emergency line loses air pressure, the tractor protection valve opens and the emergency trailer brakes activate.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a sign of fatigue?
questions.explanation: Signs of fatigue include trouble focusing, frequent blinking, heavy eyelids, repeated yawning, rubbing your eyes, daydreaming, trouble remembering the last few miles, missing exits or traffic signs, trouble keeping your head up, drifting from your lane, following too closely, hitting rumble strips, and feeling restless or irritable.

questions.question: Do not smoke within ____ of a vehicle carrying Class 3 or Division 2.1 materials.
questions.explanation: Do not smoke within 25 feet of a placarded tank carrying Class 3 (flammable liquids) or Division 2.1 (gases) materials. Also do not smoke or carry a lit cigar, cigarette, or pipe within 25 feet of vehicles carrying Class 1 (explosives), Class 4 (flammable solids), or Class 4.2 (spontaneously combustible) materials.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Move quickly before other vehicles can enter the lane.
Move slowly in case another vehicle is in the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move slowly in case another vehicle is in the lane.
questions.explanation: Always change lanes slowly and smoothly. If another vehicle is in the lane that you did not see, the driver will have more time to react to your vehicle.

questions.question: ____ identical placards must be placed on a vehicle transporting hazardous materials.
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials placards must be placed on all four sides of the vehicle.

questions.question: If you feel fatigued while driving, you should:

options.text: Drive faster to finish the trip sooner.

questions.explanation: If you feel drowsy while driving, safely leave the road and sleep. Artificial stimulants are dangerous because they can cause extreme fatigue when they wear off.
